decision_note: Focused nectar-evolution/ecology synthesis treats nectar as a multiorganism interface rather than a simple reward; retain as relevant source-chasing material for pollinators, exploiters and microbes.
Linalool article is centered on floral-fragrance biosynthesis in a pollination system and does not measure a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.
Nicotine-in-nectar experiment measures bumblebee learning of floral features without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter component.
Study compares pollinators with parasitoids sharing floral resources; parasitoids are natural enemies of herbivores rather than a plant antagonist/exploiter response to a floral coordinate.
Floral-volatile experiment tests plant–plant flowering synchronization while pollinators are excluded; pollinator/herbivore effects are discussed as context rather than measured focal responses.

Primary Dalechampia study directly tests whether seed predators constrain pollinator-mediated floral-trait evolution across populations and finds little evidence; retain as an explicit negative-control mutualist–antagonist trait study.

Primary pyrethrum study identifies a floral volatile that attracts nocturnal moths, improves pollination success and induces oviposition on a nonhost; retain for plant-mediated role/manipulation boundary adjudication.
Dieffenbachia study directly assays floral-scent attraction of florivorous plant bugs; pollinator attraction is only preliminary/contextual and is not a focal measured response in the source.
Primary Cucurbita study quantifies non-pollinating floral visitors and their relationship with pollinating-bee foraging; retain for pollinator–exploiter/interference adjudication.
Plant-pollinator network robustness preprint models antagonistic interactions at network level without a focal plant floral trait/reward coordinate.
Florivore-induced autogamy study shows Mompha feeding causes self-pollination and seed/fruit development, but no animal pollinator service/response is measured in the focal interaction.
Moth/butterfly odorant-receptor study focuses animal receptor conservation to flowering-plant cues rather than a focal plant trait with pollinator and antagonist responses.

Primary Erythronium pollen-colour study tests pollinator colour preferences, pollen-feeding beetle predation, UV tolerance and siring success; retain as a same-trait negative/one-sided geometry candidate.
Green-roof plant-composition study targets ecosystem functionality/biodiversity rather than a focal floral coordinate linking pollinator and antagonist responses.
Regional Orchidaceae floristic/taxonomic inventory is not a focal plant–pollinator–antagonist trait study.
Understory ornithophilous-plant study concerns hummingbird interactions without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter component.
Navaea study quantifies differential bird pollination efficiency without a focal antagonist/exploiter response.

Primary large-herbivore enclosure experiment shows deer herbivory reduces flower abundance and disrupts plant–pollinator network structure; retain for herbivory-mediated pollination-context adjudication.
Primary Rheum–Bradysia study examines a mutualistic seed-consuming pollinator whose oviposition reduces fruit abortion; retain for brood-pollination benefit–cost/role-boundary adjudication.
Ozone experiment tests herbivore host finding without a focal pollinator service/response.
American Journal of Botany flower-colour collection introduction is an editorial framing piece rather than an independent primary study or focused SCH synthesis.

Primary comparative Phyllantheae study documents convergent floral adaptations to obligate Epicephala moth pollination in which larvae consume developing seeds; retain for brood-pollination evolutionary/role-boundary adjudication.

Primary Ficus experiment crosses parasitic wasps with cooperative or pollen-free pollinator wasps and measures host investment/fig sanctions; retain for mutualism–parasite and plant-investment adjudication.

Primary Ficus study tests how pollinator, gallers and parasitoids exert conflicting pressures on host reproductive asynchrony in an obligate pollination mutualism; retain for multi-agent phenology adjudication.
Apocrypta study focuses parasitoid life history/parasitism ability in a fig-wasp community; pollinator abundance is a host/resource correlate rather than a focal pollination service response.
